nodes.label: data workflow job: check (make lint, test, validate, triage-all)
nodes.norm_label: data workflow job: check (make lint, test, validate, triage-all)
nodes.rationale: make triage-all is run for the log, not the gate: it prints the full trace of every demonstration consultation so the effect of a weights or ranking change is readable in the PR's CI output. --extra ingest is required because the clean-step tests import BeautifulSoup.

nodes.label: Evaluation pipeline: eval/benchmark -> make eval-cases -> eval/cases -> make eval -> build/eval
nodes.norm_label: evaluation pipeline: eval/benchmark -> make eval-cases -> eval/cases -> make eval -> build/eval

nodes.label: SOURCE.md (benchmark provenance, label vocabulary, language tie)
nodes.norm_label: source.md (benchmark provenance, label vocabulary, language tie)

nodes.label: Silver annotations read off the benchmark's reference answers
nodes.norm_label: silver annotations read off the benchmark's reference answers

nodes.label: CLI refuses values outside a feature's allowed_values
nodes.norm_label: cli refuses values outside a feature's allowed_values
nodes.rationale: A typo that reads as 'she did not say' would quietly turn an escalation into a routine appointment, so anything else is refused rather than treated as unknown.

nodes.label: Risk labels derived once from English and propagated by canonical_case_id
nodes.norm_label: risk labels derived once from english and propagated by canonical_case_id
nodes.rationale: Running English keyword rules over translated text produced language-asymmetric labels skewed toward routine last time, and the converter has to be able to prove it did not.

nodes.label: Immutable benchmark source (never edited, new versions land beside)
nodes.norm_label: immutable benchmark source (never edited, new versions land beside)
nodes.rationale: The old file is never overwritten so a result computed last month can still be reproduced, and keeping the original makes the conversion reviewable: if a label looks wrong in cases/, the sentence it came from is still there. Same pattern as evidence_batches to knowledge/evidence.csv.

nodes.label: make eval measures the controller alone, not the whole system
nodes.norm_label: make eval measures the controller alone, not the whole system
nodes.rationale: Cases are expressed as feature values, so cross-language and register agreement are unmeasurable here and clarification recall is near-vacuous (the controller cannot conclude before asking, so it always asks).

nodes.label: in_scope: false cases (excluded from scoring, counted in the report)
nodes.norm_label: in_scope: false cases (excluded from scoring, counted in the report)
nodes.rationale: Marks a case probing something deliberately not modelled, such as pregnancy-related bleeding. A gap we chose is not a gap we missed, and printing one as the other would misstate both.

nodes.label: label_quote is required and must be a real sentence from the reference answer
nodes.norm_label: label_quote is required and must be a real sentence from the reference answer
nodes.rationale: Same role as source_quote on a clinical row: it makes the label a restatement of something the benchmark says rather than the team's judgement, and it is what a second reader checks. An untraceable label is deleted, not softened.

nodes.label: Non-string YAML values are refused rather than stringified
nodes.norm_label: non-string yaml values are refused rather than stringified
nodes.rationale: 30 becoming "30" would be a silent wrong answer that scores as a triage failure rather than the typo it is.

nodes.label: A variant cannot carry a label
nodes.norm_label: a variant cannot carry a label
nodes.rationale: Labels live on the canonical case and reach every register and language through canonical_case_id. Deriving labels by running English keyword rules over translated text produced language-asymmetric labels skewed toward routine (French under-triage 0.994); here that failure is unrepresentable rather than merely forbidden.

nodes.label: deploy job: build three images, push to ECR, upload deploy files, run deploy.sh via SSM
nodes.norm_label: deploy job: build three images, push to ecr, upload deploy files, run deploy.sh via ssm
nodes.rationale: Guarded to refs/heads/main because workflow_dispatch can be started from any branch; concurrency never cancels a deploy halfway through a migration. ECR tags are immutable, so a re-run skips images that already exist for the commit.

nodes.label: backend service (herhealth-backend image, port 8000, RDS)
nodes.rationale: Secrets come from /run/herhealth/backend.env on tmpfs and reach only this container; they are read at container creation, so a rotated RDS password needs the backend recreated. The /health check pings the database but never calls OpenRouter or any external service.

nodes.label: caddy service (TLS reverse proxy, only published ports)
nodes.norm_label: caddy service (tls reverse proxy, only published ports)
nodes.rationale: The Caddyfile directory is mounted, not the file: deploy.sh replaces the file with mv, which gives it a new inode a single-file bind mount would not follow. caddy_data holds certificates and the ACME account; Let's Encrypt allows only 5 duplicate certificates per week, so caddy-data.sh backs it up to S3 before a destroy.

nodes.label: retrieval service (herhealth-retrieval image, bge-m3, port 8001)
nodes.rationale: Weights are baked into the image at a pinned revision and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 forbids reaching the hub at runtime, because a moving revision would no longer match the index's vectors. mem_limit 4g protects the host from the ~2 GB resident model.

nodes.label: ECR images: herhealth-frontend, herhealth-backend, herhealth-retrieval (SHA-tagged, immutable)
nodes.norm_label: ecr images: herhealth-frontend, herhealth-backend, herhealth-retrieval (sha-tagged, immutable)

nodes.label: Deploy through SSM Run Command (herhealth-deploy document)
nodes.norm_label: deploy through ssm run command (herhealth-deploy document)
nodes.rationale: The host runs /opt/herhealth/deploy.sh <sha>, which migrates, switches, health-checks through Caddy and rolls back to the previous tag by itself if the check fails.

nodes.label: Deploy-time index verification (model, revision, no quote-only text)
nodes.norm_label: deploy-time index verification (model, revision, no quote-only text)
nodes.rationale: Belt and braces: publish-index.sh already refused to upload quote-only text, but an image is the last place it could slip in. Also checks that the index's bge-m3 revision equals BGE_M3_REVISION, otherwise weights and vectors would not match.

nodes.label: Production runs the base model via OpenRouter only (model selector off)
nodes.norm_label: production runs the base model via openrouter only (model selector off)
nodes.rationale: The fine-tuned adapter is not cleared to own triage decisions, so HERHEALTH_TRIAGE_MODE=openrouter, HERHEALTH_MODEL_SELECTOR=off, and no VLLM_* variable exists in the file or the secrets.

nodes.label: The higher bar on concluding SELF_CARE
nodes.community_name: Case: vulval itching with discharge, no pain
nodes.norm_label: the higher bar on concluding self_care

nodes.label: Flagged feature candidate: visible or palpable vaginal bulge
nodes.norm_label: flagged feature candidate: visible or palpable vaginal bulge
nodes.rationale: The clearest and most specific prolapse finding has no feature; it is the strongest candidate for a new feature but adding a feature is a bigger decision than adding a row, so it is left to the reviewer.

nodes.label: NHS rename of PCOS to PMOS (polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome)
nodes.norm_label: nhs rename of pcos to pmos (polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome)
nodes.rationale: The old NHS slug never matched because of the rename; fetching the PMOS page gives pcos its first precedence-2 source and sources the condition's label.

nodes.label: no_red_flag_pcos_picture_case (absence of a rule must not escalate)
nodes.norm_label: no_red_flag_pcos_picture_case (absence of a rule must not escalate)
nodes.rationale: Checks the over-triage direction: no rule fires, so the differential carries it to pcos's baseline ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT.

nodes.label: ovarian_cyst's first eliminating row (difficulty_conceiving argues_against)
nodes.rationale: womenshealth directly answers 'Can ovarian cysts make it harder to get pregnant?' with 'Typically, no' and names endometriosis and PCOS as where it does apply - explicit distinguishing language that clears ADR 0001's bar. It replaced an NHS weak_support row on the same cell, which the schema rejected as a duplicate.

nodes.label: One row per (condition, feature, value) cell; prefer womenshealth when sources agree
nodes.norm_label: one row per (condition, feature, value) cell; prefer womenshealth when sources agree
nodes.rationale: The score sums weights, so a second row on one cell would double-count. Where sources agree, womenshealth is taken because it is public domain and may enter passages.parquet, while NHS is citable_only; NHS precedence only decides conflicts.

nodes.label: Lexical scan overestimated free NHS cells (41 suggested, 5 real)
nodes.norm_label: lexical scan overestimated free nhs cells (41 suggested, 5 real)
nodes.rationale: 21 of 26 checked candidates were already authored from other sources, and the scan was simply wrong on several pages; remaining NHS opportunity lies in the seven conditions with no NHS page fetched.

nodes.label: Rule-derived cases are implementation verification, not accuracy
nodes.norm_label: rule-derived cases are implementation verification, not accuracy
nodes.rationale: A case built from a rule and run against that rule shares its assumptions; it checks clause evaluation, most-severe-wins, the escalation screen and overlapping rules, not whether the rule is clinically right. Two real defects were found in that machinery on 2026-09-11, one hiding five live EMERGENCY rules.

nodes.label: Most-severe-rule-wins (sudden vs gradual severe pelvic pain pair)
nodes.norm_label: most-severe-rule-wins (sudden vs gradual severe pelvic pain pair)
nodes.rationale: The same severity answer must land on EMERGENCY with sudden onset and URGENT_SAME_DAY without it; the paired cases are the whole point of the batch.

nodes.label: Batch 26 auto-approved without a second reader (protocol departure)
nodes.norm_label: batch 26 auto-approved without a second reader (protocol departure)
nodes.rationale: The repo owner authorised auto-approval to unblock MVP testing. Quotes were script-checked verbatim against the cleaned corpus, but the judgement that each quote supports its row was not independently checked; recorded rather than left to be inferred.

nodes.label: Dead ends: MedlinePlus UTI and ovarian-cyst pages are link hubs
nodes.norm_label: dead ends: medlineplus uti and ovarian-cyst pages are link hubs
nodes.rationale: The audit flagged medlineplus as cited-but-unused for both conditions, but the pages have almost no symptom prose; recorded so nobody repeats the search. Both conditions were enriched from NHS instead.

nodes.label: Open age-threshold encoding: one weak row per qualifying age band
nodes.norm_label: open age-threshold encoding: one weak row per qualifying age band
nodes.rationale: A source naming an open threshold ('over 30', 'before 40') is encoded as a weak row on every qualifying band rather than overstated as a single age peak. Review decision 2026-08-18.

nodes.label: Missing urine_appearance feature (well-supported argues_against candidate with no cell)
nodes.norm_label: missing urine_appearance feature (well-supported argues_against candidate with no cell)
nodes.rationale: NHS: dark or smelly pee as the only symptom may just be dehydration - explicit distinguishing language, corroborated by two other sources, but no feature covers urine appearance or smell. First thing to encode if such a feature is ever added.

nodes.label: A figure inside a verbatim quote is not converted into row strength
nodes.norm_label: a figure inside a verbatim quote is not converted into row strength
nodes.rationale: 'Never invent probabilities' governs the strength the team asserts, not whether a cited sentence may contain a number ('1 in 8', '5%'). The strength stays an ordinary ordinal judgement.

nodes.label: Bladder pain vs UTI: explicit distinction the schema has nowhere to put
nodes.norm_label: bladder pain vs uti: explicit distinction the schema has nowhere to put
nodes.rationale: womenshealth states the two are not the same problem, but the distinction is about cause and antibiotic response, not a feature-value pair a user reports. No feature should be added for one condition's sake, so no argues_against row is written.

nodes.label: Infertility age_band rows deliberately not written
nodes.norm_label: infertility age_band rows deliberately not written
nodes.rationale: age_band exists to separate perimenopause from PCOS; adding weak infertility rows across the over-35 bands would give a woman in her 40s weak age support toward three conditions and blunt that separation. Flagged for the reviewer.

nodes.label: terraform job: plan (read-only role, posted to the PR, optional)
nodes.norm_label: terraform job: plan (read-only role, posted to the pr, optional)
nodes.rationale: Skipped, not failed, for fork PRs and until AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN and the two TF_VAR variables are set; a skipped job is a neutral check. The plan role is optional because ReadOnlyAccess reads the whole account.

nodes.label: terraform job: validate (fmt -check and validate for bootstrap and prod stacks, no AWS credentials)
nodes.norm_label: terraform job: validate (fmt -check and validate for bootstrap and prod stacks, no aws credentials)

nodes.label: The row not written: NHS vs womenshealth conflict on itching in bacterial vaginosis
nodes.norm_label: the row not written: nhs vs womenshealth conflict on itching in bacterial vaginosis
nodes.rationale: NHS says BV does not usually cause itching; womenshealth lists itching among BV symptoms. An argues_against row would eliminate BV (needs antibiotics) in favour of thrush (SELF_CARE) whenever itching is reported, which is under-triage, the dominant failure mode. So no row is written in either direction; cost is that itching separates the two in one direction only.

nodes.label: Systematic elimination-row (argues_against) audit, 2026-08-19
nodes.rationale: Each condition was searched for argues_against-eligible language and the outcome recorded even when empty, so the search is not repeated or silently assumed. Gaps fall into three shapes: sources never state an excluding claim (thrush), the condition is frequently silent (PID, STI, BV, adenomyosis), or a clear distinguishing sentence has no feature to land on (bladder_pain, UTI).

nodes.label: Frequently-silent conditions get no argues_against row
nodes.norm_label: frequently-silent conditions get no argues_against row
nodes.rationale: Sources describe STI (and PID, BV, adenomyosis) as often symptomless, so absence of a symptom argues against them very little, and the protocol forbids inferring argues_against from absence in a symptom list.

nodes.label: POI vs premature menopause terminology conflict (womenshealth vs MedlinePlus)
nodes.norm_label: poi vs premature menopause terminology conflict (womenshealth vs medlineplus)
nodes.rationale: The sources disagree on whether POI and premature menopause are the same thing but agree on the symptom picture, so evidence rows are unaffected. MedlinePlus's distinguishing sentence has no cell to land on because premature menopause is not modelled separately.

nodes.label: Stopping rule 1: a red flag outranks the differential
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: stopping rule 1: a red flag outranks the differential

nodes.label: Escalation screen (probe more severe rules one answer away)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: escalation screen (probe more severe rules one answer away)
nodes.rationale: Once severe pelvic pain is known, six EMERGENCY rules are each one answer from firing. As of 2026-08-19 only 5 of the 6 appear as screen probes because bleeding_heaviness is asked earlier at turn 4 after primary_ovarian_insufficiency's age_band row changed the early differential; the sixth rule is still reached.

nodes.label: Access token (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Short-lived (minutes, not days) precisely because it cannot be revoked.

nodes.label: Conversation (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: The product-facing view of a clinical object: one consultation, stored, named, revisitable and deletable.

nodes.label: Credential (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Kept separate from the user so a second kind (password, Google identity, later passkey) can be added without a migration, and so the same email address can never by itself mean the same person.

nodes.label: Health note (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Unverified free text, never treated as a symptom she is reporting now: it cannot fire a red flag and cannot carry a conclusion by itself. It reaches the reasoning model as background in the system prompt, never as a transcript turn, because she did not say it in the consultation being recorded.

nodes.label: Linking (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Permitted only when both sides are verified; an unverified local account is taken over rather than linked, because it proved nothing.

nodes.label: Patient (a word the project does not use)
nodes.norm_label: patient (a word the project does not use)
nodes.rationale: She is not under anyone's care here, and the word imports a clinical relationship the system does not have.

nodes.label: Refresh token (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Long-lived opaque secret stored server-side; the revocable half of the pair and the reason deletion can be honest.

nodes.label: Session (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Backed by a revocable refresh token so logging out and deleting an account take effect at once. The word must never be used in the Triage context.

nodes.label: User (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: One row, one human; holds email, display name and date of birth and nothing clinical. Date of birth is stored as a date, not an age_band, so the band is derived fresh on every request; a band stored at 44 would stay 40_to_44 past the birthday, and 45 separates perimenopause from PCOS.

nodes.label: Verification (Accounts term)
nodes.rationale: Proof of control of the email address by a one-time code; gates account recovery and identity linking, not access to advice.

nodes.label: Resolved: message content is encrypted at the application layer
nodes.norm_label: resolved: message content is encrypted at the application layer
nodes.rationale: Encryption at rest defends against a stolen disk; the realistic breach paths are a leaked snapshot, an over-broad grant or a credential in git history, and application-level encryption defeats all three. It does not defend against the application itself being compromised. Settled 2026-08-05.

nodes.label: Deletion (immediate, cascading, not a flag)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a grace period because a woman deleting an account on this service may be doing so because someone else can reach her device, and a reversible window is the window in which they find it.

nodes.label: Resolved: email, not phone
nodes.rationale: SIM registration in Egypt is mandatory and identity-linked, so a phone number beside a consultation mentioning a possible pregnancy or infection creates an identity-linked clinical record by construction. Settled 2026-08-05.

nodes.label: Resolved: sessions are opaque and revocable, access tokens are not
nodes.norm_label: resolved: sessions are opaque and revocable, access tokens are not
nodes.rationale: A plain JWT cannot be revoked, and 'your account will finish deleting within 24 hours' is the wrong promise on this service. Settled 2026-08-05.

nodes.label: Open question: whether the team should be able to read conversations at all
nodes.norm_label: open question: whether the team should be able to read conversations at all
nodes.rationale: A per-user key derived from her password would remove team access but breaks with Google sign-in (no password) and with password reset (which would destroy her history). Left as a documented limitation.

nodes.label: backend workflow job: app (ruff, mypy, make test-api with testcontainers PostgreSQL)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: backend workflow job: app (ruff, mypy, make test-api with testcontainers postgresql)
nodes.rationale: No services block: the PostgreSQL container is managed by the tests through testcontainers. uv sync --locked fails rather than re-resolving so CI runs the same pins as a teammate.

nodes.label: frontend workflow job: build
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: npm ci installs exactly package-lock.json and fails on drift, the npm equivalent of uv sync --locked, and refuses to silently resolve a new dependency version.

nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup

nodes.label: Frontend lint is reporting-only (continue-on-error)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: As of 2026-10-11 npm run lint reports 4 pre-existing react-hooks/set-state-in-effect errors (site-header, health-details-form, profile-settings-form, getting-started-card). Gating today would land a red build unrelated to the change under review; fix those four, then make lint block.

nodes.label: No path filter and no branch filter on the hygiene check
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: no path filter and no branch filter on the hygiene check
nodes.rationale: Every other workflow is path-filtered, which is how the 2026-09-17 contamination went unnoticed for three weeks: a root-level public/ holding another project's code and infra/envs/backend.env.bak holding three live credentials matched no filter. The payload also survived on nine stale branches, so a check guarding only main would have passed them.

nodes.author: Arora, Wei, Hicks, Bowman, Quinonero-Candela, Tsimpourlas, Sharman, Shah, Vallone, Beutel, Heidecke, Singhal (OpenAI)
nodes.norm_label: healthbench: evaluating large language models towards improved human health (arxiv 2505.08775)
nodes.rationale: Existing health evaluations are not meaningful (multiple-choice exams), not trustworthy (unvalidated against physicians) and saturated; HealthBench answers with 5,000 multi-turn conversations graded on 48,562 physician-written rubric criteria.

nodes.label: MedHELM: Holistic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Medical Tasks (arXiv 2505.23802)

nodes.norm_label: medhelm: holistic evaluation of large language models for medical tasks (arxiv 2505.23802)
nodes.rationale: Near-perfect licensing-exam scores do not reflect real clinical practice: questions do not match real settings, only 5% of evaluations use real EHR data, and about 64% focus only on exams and diagnostic tasks.

nodes.author: Edward Hu et al.
nodes.community_name: q4 arxiv 2106.09685 lora low rank adapta
nodes.norm_label: lora: low-rank adaptation of large language models (hu et al., arxiv 2106.09685)

nodes.label: Low intrinsic rank hypothesis for weight updates
nodes.author: Edward Hu et al.
nodes.community_name: q4 arxiv 2106.09685 lora low rank adapta
nodes.norm_label: low intrinsic rank hypothesis for weight updates
nodes.rationale: Inspired by findings that over-parametrised models reside on a low intrinsic dimension, the paper hypothesises the weight change during adaptation also has low intrinsic rank; a rank of one or two suffices on GPT-3 175B even when full rank is 12,288.

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (frozen W0 plus trainable BA update)
nodes.author: Edward Hu et al.
nodes.community_name: q4 arxiv 2106.09685 lora low rank adapta
nodes.norm_label: low-rank adaptation (frozen w0 plus trainable ba update)
nodes.rationale: Dense layers are trained indirectly by optimising rank-decomposition matrices of their change during adaptation while pre-trained weights stay frozen, making adaptation storage- and compute-efficient.

nodes.label: Mergeable adapters: no added inference latency
nodes.author: Edward Hu et al.
nodes.community_name: q4 arxiv 2106.09685 lora low rank adapta
nodes.norm_label: mergeable adapters: no added inference latency
nodes.rationale: The linear design lets trainable matrices be merged with the frozen weights at deployment, unlike adapter layers that extend depth or prefix methods that reduce usable sequence length.

nodes.label: One shared frozen base, many small swappable LoRA modules
nodes.author: Edward Hu et al.
nodes.norm_label: one shared frozen base, many small swappable lora modules
nodes.rationale: Freezing the shared model and swapping only matrices A and B reduces storage and task-switching overhead.

nodes.rationale: BASELINE IS URGENT, WHICH IS NEW. Every other condition here sits at ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT or below, and escalation comes only from red_flags. PID is different because the NHS routes the mere suspicion of it to urgent care: "Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if: you think you have symptoms of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)". So the condition being live in the differential is itself enough. That makes it the most important addition to the differential so far. nodes.label: Ovarian cyst [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: Baseline is routine because most cysts are harmless: NHS says they are "very common and do not usually cause any symptoms" and that "Most ovarian cysts occur naturally and go away in a few months without needing any treatment." The dangerous cases — torsion and rupture — are handled by red flags, not by the baseline. Its real value is explaining `pain_onset: sudden`, which until now had nothing to point at. NHS: "An ovarian cyst usually only causes symptoms if it splits (ruptures), is very large or twists and then blocks the blood supply to the ovaries", with pain that "can range from a dull, heavy sensation to a sudden, severe and sharp pain."

nodes.label: Automation bias
nodes.rationale: The propensity of humans to over-rely on a suggestion from an automated system; in CDS it produces errors of commission (following incorrect advice) or omission (failing to act because of not being prompted to do so).

nodes.label: SELF_CARE (severity 0)
nodes.description: Nothing suggests contact with a health service is needed now. Manage at home, and seek care if symptoms change or worsen.

nodes.label: Endometriosis [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: MedlinePlus: "Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue like the lining of the uterus grows in other places in your body." It names the main symptom as "Pelvic pain, which often happens during your period". CAVEAT: NICHD has no conditioninfo section for endometriosis — its topic page is a single paragraph — so this condition rests far more heavily on MedlinePlus than the other two. The two-source rule is satisfied in form but is thin in substance here. CDC has no endometriosis page at all.

nodes.label: Normal menstrual variation [SELF_CARE]
nodes.rationale: The only condition whose baseline is SELF_CARE, and the reason that action is reachable at all. Without it every path through the differential ends at a doctor, and the system routes a healthy user to care every time — which would show up in evaluation as near-total over-triage on normal cases, indistinguishable from a fault in the elimination logic. Grounded rather than assumed. MedlinePlus gives the ranges: "Most menstrual cycles last about 28 days, but cycles can be shorter or longer and still be normal" and "A period usually lasts three to seven days and can be light or heavy". The Office on Women's Health states the two-way version in one sentence: "Regular menstrual periods in the year

nodes.label: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.norm_label: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (pmos), formerly polycystic ovary syndrome (pcos) [routine_appointment]
nodes.rationale: MedlinePlus: "Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the name for set of symptoms that are related to an imbalance of hormones. PCOS affects the ovaries, as well as many other parts of the body." The same page states people with PCOS "usually have at least two of these problems: Not ovulating... High levels of androgens... Cysts in one or both ovaries", which is what the evidence rows key on. NICHD supplies symptom, cause and treatment pages under conditioninfo/.

nodes.label: Uterine fibroids [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: MedlinePlus: "Many women with fibroids have no symptoms. If you do, the type of symptoms may be due to location, size, and number of fibroids", listing "Heavy or painful periods or bleeding between periods" and "Feeling 'full' in the lower abdomen (belly)". The asymptomatic majority matters for elimination: absence of symptoms argues against far less strongly here than it would for a condition that is always symptomatic. NICHD supplies symptom, cause and treatment pages under conditioninfo/.

nodes.label: Dark velvety patches of skin (acanthosis_nigricans)
nodes.rationale: Named by CDC, MedlinePlus and NICHD, all of which tie it to insulin resistance in PCOS. Visually distinctive and easy for a user to recognise once described, which is why the probe describes it rather than naming it.

nodes.label: Heaviness of bleeding (bleeding_heaviness)
nodes.rationale: "soaking_hourly" is deliberately its own level rather than the top of "heavy". It is the value escalation rules key on, and collapsing it into "heavy" would lose the distinction that matters most. The clot and clothes-soaking examples come from the NHS definition of heavy periods: "need to change your pad or tampon every 1 to 2 hours", "pass blood clots larger than about 2.5cm", "bleed through to your clothes or bedding". They live in the PROBE rather than in a feature of their own, because they describe how to judge heaviness rather than being findings a source ties to any condition. The 2.5c

nodes.label: Low mood or anxiety (low_mood_or_anxiety)
nodes.rationale: Named by NHS (for both PMOS and endometriosis), MedlinePlus and NICHD. Burden 3 because it is personal, so next_question should reach it late and only when it would change the action. It is a poor discriminator on its own — it appears under several conditions — but it matters for the informational half of what this system does.

nodes.label: MTEB benchmark (8 tasks, 58 datasets, 112 languages)
nodes.rationale: Embeddings were being evaluated on a small set of datasets from a single task (mostly STS), so progress was hard to track; MTEB unifies many tasks into one accessible framework built on diversity, simplicity, extensibility and reproducibility.

nodes.label: BGE-M3 (M3-Embedding) model
nodes.rationale: Existing embedding models were English-centric, single-function and short-input; M3-Embedding targets versatility on three axes: 100+ languages, three retrieval functions, and inputs from sentences up to 8,192 tokens.

nodes.rationale: Instructions better inform the embedding model about the task; trained with an extra 500k GPT-3.5/4 synthetic examples covering 93 languages, which also expands language coverage.

nodes.label: Multilingual E5 models (mE5 small / base / large)
nodes.norm_label: multilingual e5 models (me5 small / base / large)
nodes.rationale: Most embedding models were trained only on English, limiting multilingual use; three sizes are released to trade inference efficiency against embedding quality.

nodes.norm_label: mmteb benchmark (500+ tasks, 250+ languages; mteb multilingual, indic, europe)
nodes.rationale: Existing benchmarks were constrained by language, domain and task diversity, leaving a large gap for low- and mid-resource languages; MMTEB is a community-driven expansion of MTEB to close it.

nodes.label: Qwen3 Embedding series (0.6B / 4B / 8B, Apache 2.0)

nodes.label: Finding: no single embedding method dominates across all tasks
nodes.norm_label: finding: no single embedding method dominates across all tasks
nodes.rationale: Benchmarking 33 models showed strong STS performance does not transfer to clustering or retrieval (e.g. SimCSE), so the field has not converged on a universal embedding method; model choice must be task-specific.

nodes.label: Self-knowledge distillation (integrated relevance scores as teacher signal)
nodes.norm_label: self-knowledge distillation (integrated relevance scores as teacher signal)
nodes.rationale: By the ensemble-learning principle, heterogeneous predictors (dense, sparse, multi-vector scores) combine into a stronger predictor, so their integrated score is used as the teacher signal to jointly train all three functions.

nodes.label: Two-stage training: weakly-supervised contrastive pre-training then supervised fine-tuning
nodes.norm_label: two-stage training: weakly-supervised contrastive pre-training then supervised fine-tuning
nodes.rationale: Follows the English E5 recipe: contrastive pre-training on ~1 billion multilingual text pairs, then fine-tuning on labelled data with mined hard negatives and cross-encoder knowledge distillation to raise embedding quality.

nodes.label: Matryoshka Representation Learning (truncatable embeddings, 1024 down to 32 dims)
nodes.norm_label: matryoshka representation learning (truncatable embeddings, 1024 down to 32 dims)
nodes.rationale: Modifying the training loss lets embeddings be truncated to save storage without compromising downstream performance.

nodes.label: Task-specific LoRA adapters (retrieval, clustering, classification, text matching)
nodes.norm_label: task-specific lora adapters (retrieval, clustering, classification, text matching)
nodes.rationale: Generic embeddings underperform across differing use cases; LoRA adapters need under 1% of the base weights' memory, so several task-tuned variants can ship in one model as an alternative to instruction-based methods.

nodes.label: Benchmark downsampling via inter-task correlation and hard-negative sampling
nodes.norm_label: benchmark downsampling via inter-task correlation and hard-negative sampling
nodes.rationale: Cuts compute so low-resource communities can run the benchmark while preserving relative model rankings; the zero-shot English benchmark needs only 2% of the original documents.

nodes.label: Finding: small XLM-R-based models outperform 7B LLM embedders in multilingual / low-resource settings
nodes.norm_label: finding: small xlm-r-based models outperform 7b llm embedders in multilingual / low-resource settings
nodes.rationale: Large LLM-based embedders win on English, but the best publicly available multilingual model is multilingual-e5-large-instruct at only 560M parameters; size is not the deciding factor for multilingual retrieval.

nodes.label: LLM-synthesised multilingual training data

nodes.label: Sexually transmitted infection (STI) [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: Included because it is the CAUSE of pelvic inflammatory disease — NHS: "Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is usually caused by sexually transmitted infections (STIs) like chlamydia and gonorrhoea" — and because it is what `abnormal_discharge` should point at before anything else. Baseline routine rather than urgent: NHS routes to a GP or sexual health clinic. It escalates only through PID, which carries the urgent baseline. Treated as one condition rather than one per organism: the triage action is the same for all of them, and this system decides urgency, not which organism.

nodes.label: Urinary tract infection (UTI) [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: The commonest benign cause of pelvic pain with urinary symptoms, and NHS names it first among the common causes of pelvic pain. Without it, `urinary_symptoms` pushes toward fibroids when the answer is usually far simpler — a differential that omits the common explanation will systematically over-suspect the rare one.

nodes.label: Age band (age_band)
nodes.rationale: Carries weight far beyond PCOS. Separates perimenopause from PCOS in women over 45, and makes bleeding after menopause interpretable at all.

nodes.label: Symptoms suggesting blood loss (anaemia_symptoms)
nodes.rationale: Turns "heavy bleeding" from a description into a question about whether it is having an effect, which is what moves it between routine and urgent.

nodes.label: Cycle regularity (cycle_regularity)
nodes.rationale: The single most separating question in the phase 1 differential, and the one that makes elimination work at all.

nodes.label: Extreme tiredness (extreme_tiredness)
nodes.rationale: OVERLAPS anaemia_symptoms, deliberately and with care. That feature asks about tiredness WITH breathlessness and dizziness — the picture of blood loss. This one is fatigue on its own, which the NHS lists for endometriosis ("extreme tiredness (fatigue)") and for PMOS ("feeling very tired") without any bleeding context. The two are correlated, so a user may answer yes to both and the controller would count fatigue twice. Flagged for phase 2: correlated features are a known weakness of naive log-odds accumulation, and this is the clearest instance in the set.

nodes.label: Urinary symptoms (urinary_symptoms)
nodes.rationale: Three different things in one question, in increasing urgency. Frequency suggests pressure from a mass; incontinence likewise but is separately named by NHS for fibroids ("not being able to control when you pee") and for perimenopause; difficulty passing urine does not wait and keys a red flag. `incontinence` added 2026-08-04. Adding a value is safe — no existing row referenced it — but note that a value which no evidence row uses is dead weight in the same way an unused feature is.

nodes.rationale: Risk labels are derived once from English and propagated by canonical_case_id because English keyword rules on translated text produced language-asymmetric labels.

nodes.label: evidence.csv (140-row sparse grid)
nodes.rationale: A missing row is the correct representation of 'this source does not connect these two things', not a gap to fill.

nodes.label: Five Evidence Weights (ordinal scale)

nodes.norm_label: excluded sources (nice cks, rcog/acog, umls, who icd)
nodes.rationale: NICE CKS licence is UK-only and forbids reuse without written agreement while users are in Egypt; a wall, not a barrier to clear.

nodes.label: gold_seeds_styled Benchmark (540 rows, 90 seeds x 6 registers)
nodes.norm_label: gold_seeds_styled benchmark (540 rows, 90 seeds x 6 registers)
nodes.source_location: The fine-tuned model from our evaluation paper

nodes.label: Knowledge Base (seven files under knowledge/)
nodes.rationale: Kept as plain text in git so every clinical change is a reviewable diff; source-traceable but not clinician-adjudicated.

nodes.label: NHS Website Source (citable_only)
nodes.rationale: Crown copyright with no reuse grant: text may be quoted with attribution into source_quote but must never enter passages.parquet.

nodes.label: packages/contracts (Pydantic schemas, error codes, safety policy)
nodes.norm_label: packages/contracts (pydantic schemas, error codes, safety policy)

nodes.label: primary_ovarian_insufficiency Source Conflict
nodes.rationale: womenshealth equates premature menopause with POI while MedlinePlus says they differ; authored anyway because both agree on the symptom picture.
nodes.source_location: The conditions, and where each stands

nodes.label: services/backend (FastAPI triage and orchestration)
nodes.rationale: No model weights load inside the backend process; embedding is an HTTP call to services/model.

nodes.label: Source Precedence on Conflict (NHS 2, others 3, CDC 4)
nodes.norm_label: source precedence on conflict (nhs 2, others 3, cdc 4)
nodes.rationale: Precedence decides who wins, not whether the losing side is written out; where sources contradict on whether a symptom occurs, write no row and record why.

nodes.label: sources.yaml (5 sources: precedence and status)
nodes.rationale: Only usable sources are listed; unusable ones were removed so nothing unusable can be cited by accident.

nodes.label: make verify-quotes (verbatim quote check)
nodes.rationale: Needs a complete gitignored build/clean; a missing page reports NOT_FOUND, indistinguishable from a fabricated quote, so run make fetch and make clean before trusting a failure.

nodes.label: Office on Women's Health (womenshealth.gov) Source
nodes.rationale: Public domain and ingestable, so preferred with MedlinePlus at equal precedence; an NHS-only row is citable but unretrievable.

nodes.label: Repo Hygiene Check (githooks, hygiene workflow)
nodes.rationale: The hook is a convenience; the real gate is the hygiene workflow on every push, created after the injected PostCSS payload and leaked env backup incident.

nodes.label: Batch 24 (discharge_smell, discharge_appearance)
nodes.rationale: BV, thrush and STI all shared one identical abnormal_discharge row, so discharge over-triaged toward infective reads and BV could never be raised.

nodes.label: Citations End to End (RetrievedPassage.url, cited_passages, ADR 0012)
nodes.norm_label: citations end to end (retrievedpassage.url, cited_passages, adr 0012)
nodes.rationale: Cited passages are resolved eagerly at the turn and persisted because retrieval is a live similarity search.

nodes.label: OpenRouter json_schema strict Mode Hangs
nodes.rationale: response_format json_schema strict hangs indefinitely; use json_object plus an explicit shape instruction in the prompt.

nodes.label: Intermittent Silent Hang in Triage Turn (REASONING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
nodes.norm_label: intermittent silent hang in triage turn (reasoning_timeout_seconds)
nodes.rationale: Contained, not fixed, by asyncio.wait_for with a 150 s timeout in triage routes.py; root cause still open.

nodes.label: Run the Full App Locally (Postgres, retrieval :8001, backend :8000, frontend :3000)
nodes.norm_label: run the full app locally (postgres, retrieval :8001, backend :8000, frontend :3000)
nodes.rationale: Order matters: a turn calls retrieval on :8001 before the reasoning model, so a 502/WinError 10061 almost always means :8001 is down.

nodes.label: ADR 0006 Single-Source Condition Exception (adenomyosis)
nodes.rationale: A single-source condition is admitted when the row says why; NHS names adenomyosis repeatedly alongside endometriosis.
nodes.source_location: The conditions, and where each stands

nodes.label: ADR 0007 What the First Real Consultations Showed
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007 what the first real consultations showed

nodes.label: ADR 0011 Controller-Free Triage
nodes.rationale: Accepted 2026-08-31 against the recommendation of docs/research/0001: the reasoning model decides ask-vs-conclude and the action code directly, grounded by injected red_flags.yaml and retrieved passages; the deterministic controller is retired and the gaps are named in the ADR's risk register.
nodes.source_location: Why it is built this way

nodes.label: ADR 0013 Emergency Conclusions May Name Conditions (proposed)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013 emergency conclusions may name conditions (proposed)
nodes.rationale: A product judgement: a woman sent to an emergency department is told what patterns the warning sign relates to; URGENT_SAME_DAY red flags keep the name-no-condition restriction.
nodes.source_location: The conditions, and where each stands

nodes.label: FDA Clinical Decision Support Software Guidance (29 Jan 2026)
nodes.norm_label: fda clinical decision support software guidance (29 jan 2026)
nodes.source_location: Why it is built this way

nodes.label: 10-Row Clinical Batch Review Limit
nodes.rationale: Never generate more than 10 clinical rows without stopping for human review; present as a table, wait for approval, then write.

nodes.label: Two-Question Evidence Row Authoring (listed? absence doubts?)
nodes.norm_label: two-question evidence row authoring (listed? absence doubts?)
nodes.rationale: Question 2 (would absence make you doubt the condition) is what makes elimination work; without 'regular periods argues_against PCOS', PCOS never drops out.

nodes.label: Deterministic Byte-Identical Builds
nodes.rationale: Rows sorted and keys ordered so re-running is byte-identical and a diff only ever shows a real change.

nodes.label: Licence Guards Run Before the Request
nodes.norm_label: licence guards run before the request
nodes.rationale: /ency/ on MedlinePlus is barred by path because its terms forbid ingestion into a health IT system.

nodes.label: Extract Escalation Criteria First
nodes.rationale: 'When to get help' and 'call 999' sections are clinician-authored escalation criteria and the most valuable text in any source; they become red_flags.yaml.

nodes.label: MedlinePlus /ency/ (A.D.A.M.) Path Exclusion
nodes.rationale: A.D.A.M. terms forbid ingesting the content into an EHR, patient portal or other health IT system, which names systems like this one.

nodes.label: argues_against Only When Source Is Explicit
nodes.norm_label: argues_against only when source is explicit
nodes.rationale: Sources rarely state what argues against a condition; do not infer from absence in a symptom list; a missing row is neutral, which is safe.

nodes.label: bge-m3 Sentence-Level Retrieval, No Reranker (ADR 0010)
nodes.rationale: Multilingual encoders beat Arabic-specific ones in published Arabic RAG results; sentence-level chunking is load-bearing for verify-quotes; reranker deferred until evaluation shows the right passage ranked outside top k.

nodes.label: Cancers Deliberately Absent from Conditions
nodes.rationale: Modelling cancers invites suggesting cancer to a worried user; they are served by red flags (bleeding_after_menopause) that escalate without naming why.
nodes.source_location: The conditions, and where each stands

nodes.label: Compensating Controls (conservative bias)
nodes.rationale: Unreviewed content means biasing conservative: red flags only from explicit escalation language, SELF_CARE bar strictly higher than ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT, conflicts take the higher urgency.

nodes.label: Escalation Screen (probe for more severe rule one answer away)
nodes.norm_label: escalation screen (probe for more severe rule one answer away)
nodes.rationale: A fired rule does not conclude while a strictly more severe rule is one answer away; it has no probe budget because a budget would silently drop the last emergency rules.

nodes.label: Cross-Service Import Rule (contracts only, import-linter)
nodes.rationale: Nothing outside packages/contracts may be imported across service boundaries; a service needing another service's code means it belongs in contracts or the boundary is wrong.

nodes.label: English-Only Probe Language Scope
nodes.rationale: Probes are authored in English only; the multilingual serving model renders them at response time; schema must allow fr/ar keys later without migration.

nodes.label: Never Diagnoses Rule
nodes.rationale: The system does urgency triage and informational guidance only; no file, comment, string, commit or UI copy may describe it as diagnosing.

nodes.label: Never Invent (probabilities, citations, ICD-11 codes)
nodes.rationale: Ordinal weights only; no source, no row; ICD-11 codes recalled from training data are unreliable so write TODO_VERIFY.

nodes.label: Frontend Is Not a PWA
nodes.rationale: No service worker, manifest, offline shell, install prompt or web push; do not add or suggest PWA scaffolding.

nodes.label: Seven Red-Flag-Only Features (no evidence rows)
nodes.rationale: They exist to fire escalation rules, not to raise a condition; do not fill them in.

nodes.label: Red-Flag Recall (provable gate becomes measured rate)
nodes.norm_label: red-flag recall (provable gate becomes measured rate)
nodes.rationale: Recall == 1.0 was provable only because the controller evaluated every clause by code; once the model must notice injected red-flag text it is a measured rate.

nodes.label: Under-Triage as Dominant Failure Mode (prefer false alarms)
nodes.norm_label: under-triage as dominant failure mode (prefer false alarms)
nodes.rationale: Whenever a design choice trades false alarms against missed escalations, choose false alarms; independently described by the FDA as automation-bias errors of omission.
nodes.source_location: Why it is built this way

nodes.label: Verification Protocol (replaces clinician review)
nodes.rationale: No clinician reviewer is available, so every row must restate a cited source sentence; verification becomes a reading-comprehension task the team can perform.

nodes.label: Knowledge Changes Never Share a PR with Code
nodes.norm_label: knowledge changes never share a pr with code
nodes.rationale: Revertability: a wrong evidence row or red-flag threshold must be revertable without also reverting the parser, validator or API change.
nodes.source_location: Two rules specific to this repo

nodes.label: Secrets Policy (*.env, *.bak gitignored; rotate on leak)
nodes.norm_label: secrets policy (*.env, *.bak gitignored; rotate on leak)
nodes.rationale: A *.env-only glob missed backend.env.bak and put live keys on main for three weeks; deleting the line is not enough because git keeps it, so rotate.

nodes.label: Trunk-Based Branching (under two days, squash merge)
nodes.norm_label: trunk-based branching (under two days, squash merge)
nodes.rationale: Git-flow cannot coexist with a two-day branch limit; a week-old branch will conflict with knowledge files or the lockfile; squash gives one-commit reverts and the fix path equals the feature path.

nodes.label: uv and Committed uv.lock as Environment Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: uv and committed uv.lock as environment source of truth
nodes.rationale: uv pins Python version, transitive dependencies and local package linking; CI runs uv sync --locked so drift fails loudly rather than silently re-resolving.

nodes.label: Open Question: Collect Age Band at Sign-Up
nodes.norm_label: open question: collect age band at sign-up
nodes.rationale: Age would help separate perimenopause, PCOS and POI, but it is personal data with consequences for the privacy story and DATASHEET.

nodes.label: Knowledge Depth, Not Breadth
nodes.rationale: A new condition with one row reproduces the BV defect fixed in batch 24; deepen the thinnest conditions first.

nodes.label: Pre-ADR-0011 Stance: No Fine-Tuning, Decision Lives in Python
nodes.norm_label: pre-adr-0011 stance: no fine-tuning, decision lives in python
nodes.rationale: README still states RAG plus a deterministic controller with the model used for language, not judgement; this predates the controller-free decision recorded in CLAUDE.md.
nodes.source_location: Why it is built this way

nodes.label: Roadmap Phases 1-4
nodes.rationale: Elimination is evaluated on three hand-written conditions before anything is ingested; if it does not work at three, ten thousand scraped passages will not fix it.

nodes.label: FallbackReasoningClient (base model fallback)
nodes.rationale: When the adapter is unreachable or produces nothing valid after three retries it re-asks OpenRouter's base model; the fallback is not surfaced to the user or recorded on the turn.

nodes.label: bootstrap_multi_turn.jsonl Retrain Bootstrap Data
nodes.source_location: The fine-tuned model from our evaluation paper

nodes.label: AWS Deploy Pipeline (ECR, S3, SSM, single EC2, Caddy)
nodes.norm_label: aws deploy pipeline (ecr, s3, ssm, single ec2, caddy)
nodes.rationale: Production runs the Base model via OpenRouter only; the index is built with NHS quote-only passages excluded so NHS text never reaches S3 or an image; nothing is edited on the server.

nodes.label: ft_corpus_v1.jsonl Adaptation Corpus (2,700 rows)
nodes.rationale: All rows carry one fixed 'answer the question' instruction, which is the mechanical explanation for clarification-seeking collapsing to 0.000.
nodes.source_location: The fine-tuned model from our evaluation paper

nodes.label: QLoRA Adapter herhealth-lora-v2 (phrasing-only)
nodes.rationale: A genuine asset for six-register phrasing but must not choose an action code until retrained on multi-turn data, because its training data has no example where the right move is a clarifying question.
nodes.source_location: The fine-tuned model from our evaluation paper

nodes.label: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B Base Model (multimodal hybrid)
nodes.source_location: The base is a multimodal hybrid, not a text model

nodes.label: Training Repo Mazen-Bahgat/HerHealthGPT (branch hassan-pc)
nodes.source_location: The fine-tuned model from our evaluation paper

nodes.label: Lobot Jupyter Proxy to Campus vLLM
nodes.norm_label: lobot jupyter proxy to campus vllm
nodes.source_location: Reach campus from the laptop (Jupyter proxy)

nodes.label: HERHEALTH_MODEL_SELECTOR (off by default, ADR 0016)
nodes.rationale: The Fine-tuned option is absent, not merely unlabelled, in any shown deployment; default_model_id resolves to the base model.

nodes.label: --disable-custom-all-reduce Fix for '!!!!' NaN Output
nodes.rationale: vLLM custom all-reduce corrupts activations over a broken GPU P2P link until logits are NaN and the sampler emits token 0 ('!'); also deadlocks startup.
nodes.source_location: The base is a multimodal hybrid, not a text model

nodes.label: vLLM Serving Constraints (text-only caps, max_model_len 8192)
nodes.rationale: Image and video must both be capped to zero; the triage system prompt is ~3,200-3,600 tokens before retrieval so 4096 leaves nothing to generate into.
nodes.source_location: The base is a multimodal hybrid, not a text model

nodes.label: Data pipeline: fetch -> clean -> build -> validate -> eval
nodes.norm_label: data pipeline: fetch -> clean -> build -> validate -> eval
nodes.rationale: Knowledge is hand-authored and evaluated on three conditions before the corpus is built: if elimination does not work at three conditions, ten thousand passages will not fix it.

nodes.label: Evaluation harness (herhealth-eval / make eval), gated vs reported metrics
nodes.norm_label: evaluation harness (herhealth-eval / make eval), gated vs reported metrics
nodes.rationale: Aggregate accuracy hid the safety failure, so under-triage and red-flag recall gate; an unmeasured gated metric is a failure and agreement never reports alone.

nodes.label: fetch_all policy order: licence guard, already present, dry run, fetch
nodes.norm_label: fetch_all policy order: licence guard, already present, dry run, fetch
nodes.rationale: The licence guard runs before any network call so a barred URL cannot be requested by a retry, redirect or bug; only a real 200 with a body is written.

nodes.label: Immutable TriageState / Decision / StopReason
nodes.rationale: A consultation is a list of states that can be replayed, making scripted dialogues reproducible and explainable.

nodes.label: ingest.lock.jsonl: tracked lockfile for source content
nodes.norm_label: ingest.lock.jsonl: tracked lockfile for source content
nodes.rationale: raw/ is gitignored, so the lockfile is the only version-controlled evidence of which documents the knowledge base was built from; a changed content_hash surfaces upstream drift in a diff.

nodes.label: Invariants and where each is enforced
nodes.norm_label: invariants and where each is enforced
nodes.rationale: None of the rules relies on anyone remembering them.

nodes.label: knowledge.py Pydantic schemas (Feature, Condition, EvidenceRow, RedFlagRule, Source, Weights, Actions, KnowledgeBase)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge.py pydantic schemas (feature, condition, evidencerow, redflagrule, source, weights, actions, knowledgebase)
nodes.rationale: The schemas are the definition and the YAML/CSV conform to them; extra=forbid turns a typo into a load failure rather than a silently dropped field.

nodes.label: RawStore: immutable raw/{source}/{date}/ store bound to one date
nodes.norm_label: rawstore: immutable raw/{source}/{date}/ store bound to one date
nodes.rationale: save() refuses to overwrite so immutability is enforced, not assumed; binding to a date removes any way to write into a past snapshot.

nodes.label: Backend triage core vs app layer separation
nodes.norm_label: backend triage core vs app layer separation
nodes.rationale: The controller must run from a test or CLI with no server, GPU or network, which is what makes the evaluation harness possible; test_boundary.py enforces Triage never imports the app layer.

nodes.label: TriageEngine.should_stop: six stopping rules, first match wins
nodes.norm_label: triageengine.should_stop: six stopping rules, first match wins
nodes.rationale: The order is the policy; three places choose the more urgent option (most severe red flag, most urgent differential member, strictly higher SELF_CARE bar).

nodes.label: Build time vs request time use of the seven knowledge files
nodes.norm_label: build time vs request time use of the seven knowledge files

nodes.label: Deterministic controller being removed
nodes.rationale: The old controller caught every red-flag case provably; the reasoning model has to notice the injected list, which is a weaker kind of promise.

nodes.label: Retraining on multi-turn data (bootstrap_dataset.py, bootstrap_multi_turn.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Original training data never included an example of asking a follow-up question, so without retraining the model would answer immediately.

nodes.label: Benchmark findings (under-triage 0.718, clarification 0.856 -> 0.000, FR/AR 0.994)
nodes.rationale: These findings forced the design; consistency improved during the collapse, so consistency is never reported alone.

nodes.norm_label: how a consultation runs (model extracts, controller decides, model phrases)

nodes.label: Evidence grid: sparse, keyed by (condition_id, feature_id, value)
nodes.norm_label: evidence grid: sparse, keyed by (condition_id, feature_id, value)
nodes.rationale: The triple key makes the file a grid rather than a list of opinions; neutral is expressed by omission so 'found nothing' and 'does not matter' cannot be confused.

nodes.label: Five evidence strengths and their log-odds
nodes.norm_label: five evidence strengths and their log-odds
nodes.rationale: argues_against is deliberately weaker than weak_support: the system should gain belief faster than it loses it because wrongly dropping a condition costs more than one more question.

nodes.label: Five sources and their licence positions
nodes.norm_label: five sources and their licence positions
nodes.rationale: Unusable sources are removed rather than listed so nothing unusable can be cited by accident.

nodes.label: Knowledge schema (ER model, foreign keys, invariants)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge schema (er model, foreign keys, invariants)
nodes.rationale: Four unsafe states are unrepresentable by construction; there is deliberately no reviewed_by_clinician field.

nodes.label: Knowledge base limitations (not clinician-adjudicated, cancers absent, weak elimination)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge base limitations (not clinician-adjudicated, cancers absent, weak elimination)

nodes.label: Log-odds scoring and plausibility conversion
nodes.rationale: Percentages do not add; log-odds add meaningfully, start at 'no idea' (0.5) and are symmetric.

nodes.label: Question-condition graph with typed weighted edges
nodes.norm_label: question-condition graph with typed weighted edges

nodes.label: The stopping controller: six rules in order
nodes.norm_label: the stopping controller: six rules in order
nodes.rationale: Every tie goes to caution: most urgent member of an unresolved differential, higher SELF_CARE bar, probe for a more severe red flag.

nodes.label: Threshold fragility found by make thresholds
nodes.norm_label: threshold fragility found by make thresholds
nodes.rationale: stop_confidence clears one weak row by only 0.019 log-odds; robust alternatives exist but changing a threshold belongs with the evaluation set.

nodes.label: Thresholds (plausibility_floor, stop_confidence, self_care_stop_confidence, stop_margin, max_questions)
nodes.rationale: All chosen by the team, not calibrated; one passing mention must never conclude, and SELF_CARE must be hardest to reach because 72% of benchmark failures were that conclusion reached too easily.

nodes.label: make verify-quotes: every quote verbatim in its source
nodes.norm_label: make verify-quotes: every quote verbatim in its source

nodes.label: Standing limitation: source-traceable, not clinician-adjudicated; silver labels
nodes.norm_label: standing limitation: source-traceable, not clinician-adjudicated; silver labels

nodes.label: Headline finding: elimination barely works
nodes.rationale: argues_against may only be written where a source frames a feature as distinguishing, and patient-facing sources almost never do; inventing such rows is the failure the protocol exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Errors found and corrected (non-verbatim quotes, mis-mapped rows)
nodes.norm_label: errors found and corrected (non-verbatim quotes, mis-mapped rows)
nodes.rationale: Text that reads correctly but cannot be found in its source was not catchable by careful reading, which is why the check became a pipeline stage.

nodes.label: Phase 1 limitations (untuned thresholds, single-source adenomyosis, English-only probes)
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 limitations (untuned thresholds, single-source adenomyosis, english-only probes)

nodes.label: Ready for Phase 2: mapping action codes onto benchmark risk labels first
nodes.norm_label: ready for phase 2: mapping action codes onto benchmark risk labels first

nodes.norm_label: scope grew from three conditions to twelve before the reasoning core ran
nodes.rationale: Each addition was justified individually, but enrichment is easier to justify step by step than to stop.

nodes.norm_label: triage core uml (knowledgebase, triageengine, triagestate, decision)

nodes.norm_label: end-to-end data flow from sources to gated metrics

nodes.norm_label: make commands (fetch, clean, evidence, validate, verify-quotes, triage, eval)

nodes.norm_label: monorepo shape (contracts, data, backend, model, frontend, knowledge)

nodes.norm_label: known problems carried (nothing leaves the differential, everything returns urgent_same_day)

nodes.norm_label: deliberately after the mvp (fine-tuning, blocked conditions, cycle data)

nodes.norm_label: three parallel tracks (knowledge & evaluation, retrieval & model, api & frontend)

nodes.label: ADR 0002: Nested knowledge files are YAML; the evidence grid is CSV
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: nested knowledge files are yaml; the evidence grid is csv

nodes.label: ADR 0003: evidence.csv is generated from approved batches
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003: evidence.csv is generated from approved batches

nodes.label: make tables (generated flat exports, gitignored, never read back)
nodes.norm_label: make tables (generated flat exports, gitignored, never read back)
nodes.rationale: Two representations of the same data in version control eventually drift, so exports are generated only.

nodes.label: Mixed knowledge formats: YAML for nested files, CSV for the evidence grid
nodes.norm_label: mixed knowledge formats: yaml for nested files, csv for the evidence grid
nodes.rationale: Six files hold nested values that YAML represents natively; the evidence grid is a wide flat table of scalar rows where a one-row-per-line diff is what a clinical-grid review needs.

nodes.label: Approved-batch review gate (approved: true)
nodes.rationale: The review gate is enforced by code rather than memory: an unread draft batch cannot reach the knowledge base, so drafting ahead of review is safe by construction.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit evidence.csv
nodes.rationale: Source quotes contain commas and nested quotation marks; one stray character silently changes a clinical claim or shifts columns. Edits go to the batch file.

nodes.label: Import rule: nothing outside packages/contracts crosses a service boundary
nodes.norm_label: import rule: nothing outside packages/contracts crosses a service boundary
nodes.rationale: Both services need the shared schemas and loader, and neither may depend on the other; a thing two services need belongs in contracts.

nodes.label: Design rules: make the rule structural, fail loudly, inject the awkward dependency
nodes.norm_label: design rules: make the rule structural, fail loudly, inject the awkward dependency
nodes.rationale: Wherever a protocol rule could be enforced by a type, a signature or a raise, it is; code is read by markers, so boring and readable beats clever.

nodes.label: Escalation screen: probe a more severe rule one answer away
nodes.norm_label: escalation screen: probe a more severe rule one answer away
nodes.rationale: Without it a one-clause URGENT_SAME_DAY rule pre-empts the EMERGENCY rule one question behind it; it is bounded structurally and deliberately runs past max_questions because emergency screening is not a patience budget.

nodes.label: CLI exit codes 0/1/2 and loud stubs
nodes.norm_label: cli exit codes 0/1/2 and loud stubs
nodes.rationale: A validation step that silently approves everything is worse than no validation step.

nodes.label: Licence guards (excluded_path_fragments, e.g. MedlinePlus /ency/)
nodes.rationale: A rule that lives only in someone's memory eventually gets broken; A.D.A.M. terms bar ingestion into a health IT system.

nodes.label: ScriptedAnswers: a case is a lookup, not a script of turns
nodes.norm_label: scriptedanswers: a case is a lookup, not a script of turns
nodes.rationale: An ordered list of answers would bake the question order into the fixture and hide the thing under test; validation stops an unrecognised value reading like an honest unknown.

nodes.label: Transport injection: http_get is the only function that opens a socket
nodes.norm_label: transport injection: http_get is the only function that opens a socket
nodes.rationale: Makes 'tests never hit the network' a structural property rather than a remembered rule.

nodes.label: Two loaders: strict load_knowledge_base and the lenient validator
nodes.norm_label: two loaders: strict load_knowledge_base and the lenient validator
nodes.rationale: A runtime caller must fail on the first problem (a half-loaded differential is more dangerous than none); make validate must collect every problem with context. Merging them would make one job worse.

nodes.label: Per-source user agents, no browser impersonation
nodes.norm_label: per-source user agents, no browser impersonation
nodes.rationale: CDC's WAF allowlists client tokens; the project works around the WAF but does not impersonate a browser, and a test asserts it.

nodes.label: Red-flag rules are conjunction only (no any_of)
nodes.norm_label: red-flag rules are conjunction only (no any_of)
nodes.rationale: An 'or' is two rules so each keeps its own source_quote; a disjunction would let one quote justify a rule firing on something the source never said.

nodes.label: Independent logistic, not softmax
nodes.rationale: Softmax always floats something to the top and cannot express 'none of these fit'; under sigmoid each weight keeps a fixed odds-multiplier reading.

nodes.label: Verification protocol: every row restates a cited source
nodes.norm_label: verification protocol: every row restates a cited source
nodes.rationale: No clinician reviewer is available, so verification becomes a reading-comprehension task the team can actually perform.

nodes.label: Two lockfiles: ingest.lock.jsonl and content.lock.jsonl
nodes.rationale: The raw-byte hash proved useless for drift detection, changing on 14 of 19 documents with no clinical change.

nodes.label: evidence.csv is generated from approved batches
nodes.norm_label: evidence.csv is generated from approved batches
nodes.rationale: Hand-edits are silently overwritten and bypass review; the batch file is the only way in.

nodes.label: Evaluation cases must be translated to French and Arabic
nodes.norm_label: evaluation cases must be translated to french and arabic
nodes.rationale: The thesis is that models degrade in Arabic and French; an English-only test set cannot measure per-language under-triage or cross-language agreement.

nodes.label: Log-Odds to Plausibility Conversion (scoring.py, ADR 0005)
nodes.rationale: Evidence accumulates as log-odds while thresholds are authored on 0-1; the conversion is an independent logistic per condition.

nodes.label: Session (Accounts-only term)
nodes.rationale: A consultation's state is a replayable value; a Session type in the triage core means Accounts has leaked across the boundary.

nodes.label: Triage Bounded Context
nodes.rationale: The triage core must stay runnable with no server, database or user, which is what makes the evaluation harness possible.

nodes.label: Plausibility
nodes.rationale: Computed per condition from its own evidence alone so conditions do not compete; not a probability of the user having anything.

nodes.label: PMOS (formerly PCOS; id stays pcos)
nodes.rationale: The id remains pcos because ids are internal keys and renaming would rewrite every evidence row and break the benchmark labels.

nodes.label: Context Boundary (Accounts depends on Triage, never reverse)
nodes.norm_label: context boundary (accounts depends on triage, never reverse)
nodes.rationale: No Triage module may import from Accounts; the two meet only at the API layer that starts a consultation for an authenticated user and stores the result.

nodes.label: Open Question: Thresholds Probably Too Low
nodes.norm_label: open question: thresholds probably too low
nodes.rationale: One strong_support row reaches 0.818 and clears stop_confidence 0.65 alone, so the controller could stop after one answer; left as authored to be set by the evaluation set.

nodes.label: rules_out does not eliminate regardless of accumulated support
nodes.norm_label: rules_out does not eliminate regardless of accumulated support
nodes.rationale: Weights simply add, so prior support above +1.06 log-odds survives a rules_out row; recorded rather than patched because the fix is a real choice.

nodes.label: argues_against (-0.5 log-odds)
nodes.rationale: Only when a source explicitly frames the feature as distinguishing or excluding. Deliberately weaker than weak_support: wrongly dropping a condition costs more than asking one more question.

nodes.label: max_questions (6)
nodes.rationale: A judgement about user patience, not a statistical result. One question per turn.

nodes.label: neutral (0.0, row omitted)
nodes.rationale: Pinned to 0; absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. A neutral row is an omitted row.

nodes.label: plausibility_floor (0.05)
nodes.rationale: Below this a condition is no longer live. Too high and rare conditions vanish before being asked about; too low and the controller keeps separating conditions nobody believes in.

nodes.label: rules_out (-4.0 log-odds)
nodes.rationale: Eliminates only from a standing start; weights add, so a single strong_support row survives it. No rules_out row exists yet; read ADR 0009 before authoring the first.

nodes.label: self_care_stop_confidence (0.85)
nodes.rationale: The most important number in the file: strictly higher than stop_confidence and schema-enforced, because under-triage is the dominant failure mode (72% of see-a-doctor cases routed to routine on the benchmark).

nodes.label: stop_confidence (0.65)
nodes.rationale: Bar for stopping at ROUTINE/URGENT/EMERGENCY. Known tuning problem: a single strong_support row (0.818) clears it, probably too eager; raising toward 0.90 is the first tuning experiment.

nodes.label: stop_margin (0.15)
nodes.rationale: Guards against stopping while two conditions with different actions are neck and neck.

nodes.label: strong_support (+1.5 log-odds)
nodes.rationale: A source describes this as a main or characteristic sign; x4.5, the conventional 'moderate increase' band. No 'conclusive' level exists because one sentence from a public health page is not conclusive.

nodes.label: weak_support (+0.6 log-odds)
nodes.rationale: A source lists it among the features of the condition; x1.8, 'small but sometimes important'.

nodes.label: ADR 0005: plausibility is an independent logistic
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005: plausibility is an independent logistic

nodes.label: ADR 0009: rules_out does not override accumulated support
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009: rules_out does not override accumulated support

nodes.label: actions.yaml (four urgency actions)
nodes.rationale: Descriptions are deliberately locale-neutral: sources are UK/US, users are in Egypt, so service references are stripped and resolved per locale at response time. Severity is what cross-language comparison runs on, never text similarity.

nodes.label: knowledge/ README
nodes.rationale: Clinician sign-off is out of scope; the citation trail (source_id resolving to a real fetched document) stands in as correctness evidence. Nothing here is clinician-adjudicated. The system performs urgency triage and never diagnoses.

nodes.label: weights.yaml (ordinal-to-log-odds mapping and stopping thresholds)
nodes.rationale: Every number was chosen by the team; none is measured, sourced or clinically validated. Do not cite or call them calibrated. Changes belong in their own commit with the motivating evaluation result.

nodes.label: Cross-language comparison on action code severity
nodes.norm_label: cross-language comparison on action code severity
nodes.rationale: A model that collapses onto one answer in every language scores perfectly on text consistency while being maximally unsafe, so agreement is on action codes only.

nodes.label: Locale-neutral action codes resolved at response time
nodes.norm_label: locale-neutral action codes resolved at response time
nodes.rationale: Source content is UK and US; users are in Egypt. A string naming a phone number, service or building in this file is wrong.

nodes.label: Provenance as correctness evidence (no clinician review)
nodes.norm_label: provenance as correctness evidence (no clinician review)
nodes.rationale: Every clinical row carries a source_id resolving to a real fetched document; an unsupported row is omitted rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Red flags derive only from explicit escalation language
nodes.norm_label: red flags derive only from explicit escalation language
nodes.rationale: A rule that cannot be traced to a specific sentence is not written. Rejected 2026-08-19: anaemia symptoms alone, soaking_hourly bleeding alone, and the womenshealth ovarian-cyst faintness box (gated on a prior diagnosis the schema cannot express).

nodes.label: Plausibility as an independent logistic (not softmax)
nodes.norm_label: plausibility as an independent logistic (not softmax)
nodes.rationale: Conditions do not compete for a fixed total, so all may be implausible at once. A softmax would let the least-bad condition emerge for an unmodelled illness; with normal_variation at SELF_CARE that would manufacture under-triage.

nodes.label: Ordinal scale spacing follows evidence-based-medicine convention
nodes.norm_label: ordinal scale spacing follows evidence-based-medicine convention
nodes.rationale: The claim is about the ruler, not the rows: no row has a measured likelihood ratio; rows stay ordinal.

nodes.label: Red-flag recall must stay 100% through retuning
nodes.norm_label: red-flag recall must stay 100% through retuning
nodes.rationale: Gated in CI and never traded off against question count.

nodes.label: Under-triage is the dominant failure mode
nodes.norm_label: under-triage is the dominant failure mode
nodes.rationale: Concluding 'nothing to do' is the conclusion most costly to get wrong, so it must be the hardest to reach.

nodes.label: Adenomyosis [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: NHS distinguishes it from endometriosis explicitly — "Endometriosis is a different condition where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows in other places, such as the ovaries or fallopian tubes" — which is rare and useful, since the two present almost identically.

nodes.label: Bacterial vaginosis [ROUTINE_APPOINTMENT]
nodes.rationale: Routine rather than self-care because, unlike thrush, it needs prescribed antibiotics. The pairing matters more than either condition alone: thrush and bacterial vaginosis are the two benign explanations for discharge, and distinguishing them from each other is less important here than distinguishing both from PID.

nodes.label: Vaginal thrush (yeast infection) [SELF_CARE]
nodes.rationale: ONLY THE SECOND CONDITION WITH A SELF_CARE BASELINE, after normal_variation — and unlike that one, this is an actual illness. Justified because NHS treats it as self-manageable: thrush is treated with pharmacy antifungals without needing an appointment. That makes it the first route to SELF_CARE for a user who genuinely has something wrong, rather than for a user who has nothing wrong. Worth watching in evaluation: a SELF_CARE baseline on a real condition is exactly where under-triage would show up if the reasoning is off.

nodes.label: What the discharge looks like (discharge_appearance)
nodes.rationale: Added 2026-09-02 alongside discharge_smell, and for the same reason. The two are asked separately because the sources state them separately: NHS gives BV's smell and its consistency as two distinct symptom bullets. That is an observation about how the pages are written, and nothing more is claimed here about how the two findings co-occur — no source consulted states that. Absence of discharge is abnormal_discharge: no, not a value here. "other" carries no evidence row, as above.

nodes.label: Whether the discharge has a smell (discharge_smell)
nodes.norm_label: whether the discharge has a smell (discharge_smell)
nodes.rationale: Added 2026-09-02. vulval_itching was supposed to separate thrush from bacterial vaginosis and only half worked: it raises thrush, but the row that would have distinguished BV was blocked by the source conflict recorded above. So BV kept a single evidence row — abnormal_discharge, the same row thrush and STI both carry — and could never be raised above them. Smell is the discriminator the sources actually agree on. "fishy" is BV and "none" is thrush. Both sources state each, in their own wording rather than identical wording — NHS "a strong fishy smell" beside womenshealth "a strong fish-like o

nodes.norm_label: itching or soreness around the vulva (vulval_itching)
nodes.rationale: Added 2026-08-04 to separate the two benign causes of discharge from each other. abnormal_discharge is a yes/no, so it cannot distinguish thrush ("white vaginal discharge (often like cottage cheese), which does not usually smell") from bacterial vaginosis ("an unusual vaginal discharge that has a strong fishy smell, particularly after sex") — but itching can: the Office on Women's Health calls "extreme itchiness" the most common symptom of thrush.
