nodes.label: argues_against rows only when a source frames a feature as distinguishing
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: argues_against rows only when a source frames a feature as distinguishing
nodes.rationale: Sources list what a condition causes and rarely what argues against it; absence from a symptom list is never grounds for a row.

nodes.label: No reviewed_by_clinician field (extra=forbid, pinned by test)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: no reviewed_by_clinician field (extra=forbid, pinned by test)
nodes.rationale: Such a field could only hold a value the team is not in a position to assert; a test rejects any field matching clinic|review|approv.

nodes.label: Source-traceability rule (every row restates a cited source)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: source-traceability rule (every row restates a cited source)
nodes.rationale: No clinician reviewer is available, so the knowledge base is constrained to restatements of cited sources carrying the verbatim sentence; this turns verification from a medical task into a reading-comprehension task the team can perform.

nodes.label: Default rule: take the higher urgency when sources conflict
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: default rule: take the higher urgency when sources conflict
nodes.rationale: ADR 0004 is a deliberate, recorded departure from this default; it is the single largest over-triage lever in the rule set and must be revisited if pain_getting_worse or pain_on_movement features are added.

nodes.label: severe_pelvic_pain red flag resolves to URGENT_SAME_DAY
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: severe_pelvic_pain red flag resolves to urgent_same_day
nodes.rationale: Three equal-precedence NHS pages disagree; the 999 bullet is 'severe, getting worse, or hurts on movement/touch' (an acute abdomen), not severity alone, and routing all severe pain to an ambulance would fire constantly on the endometriosis and fibroid population.

nodes.label: single_source_reason exception to the two-source rule
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: single_source_reason exception to the two-source rule
nodes.rationale: The two-source rule exists so no condition rests on one document; NHS names adenomyosis across three pages, and omitting it would attribute those symptoms to endometriosis. The exception is deliberately awkward: it can only be taken by writing an argument a reviewer reads.

nodes.label: Escalation screen / escalation probing (most severe rule wins; probe rules one answer away)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: escalation screen / escalation probing (most severe rule wins; probe rules one answer away)
nodes.rationale: A fired red flag was pre-empting a more severe one a single question away (sudden_severe_pain.yaml returned URGENT_SAME_DAY instead of EMERGENCY); the fix follows the standing tie-break of choosing false alarms over missed escalations.

nodes.label: Finding 1: nothing ever leaves the differential
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: finding 1: nothing ever leaves the differential
nodes.rationale: Every condition starts at 0.50 plausibility and 8 of 12 conditions have zero eliminating rows, so all conditions stay live; this is what the knowledge base supports, not a code bug.

nodes.label: Finding 2: question selection barely depends on answers (_separation is answer-independent)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: finding 2: question selection barely depends on answers (_separation is answer-independent)
nodes.rationale: _separation sums absolute weight a feature could apply without modelling which answer is likely, so the controller runs a near-fixed questionnaire; vulval_itching was never asked in an itching case.

nodes.label: Finding 3: every consultation returns URGENT_SAME_DAY
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.rationale: Rule 5 stops at the most urgent live member, and pelvic_inflammatory_disease is always live; a system that says 'be seen today' to everyone has perfect recall and no information content.

nodes.label: No probe budget: the screen deliberately runs past max_questions
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: no probe budget: the screen deliberately runs past max_questions
nodes.rationale: The bound comes from the knowledge base (each probe fires or kills its rule); a budget low enough to protect patience would silently drop the last emergency rules. Cost: ten questions instead of four in the severe-pain case.

nodes.label: Alignment block (what symptoms overlap with, cited, never a diagnosis)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: alignment block (what symptoms overlap with, cited, never a diagnosis)
nodes.rationale: Mentors asked for guidance to feel informative; the sentence is about the source and the symptom, never the user and a condition, because every row only says 'condition X causes symptom Y' and reading it backwards is an inference the sources do not make.

nodes.label: QLoRA adapter must be retrained on multi-turn data before it decides anything
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: qlora adapter must be retrained on multi-turn data before it decides anything
nodes.rationale: The adapter saw only complete answers and no clarifying question, the documented cause of clarification collapsing from 0.856 to 0.000; handing it the decision unretrained would likely reproduce the collapse.

nodes.label: Agentic RAG (model-directed retrieve-then-reason loop)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.rationale: Triage is inherently multi-turn; the pattern combines a dedicated embedding model with a reasoning fine-tune and reuses existing retrieval code. Its best-documented failure, stopping early or never asking, is the same risk MediQ and the project's own benchmark measured.

nodes.label: Decision: remove the deterministic controller; the reasoning model decides ask-vs-conclude and the action code
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: decision: remove the deterministic controller; the reasoning model decides ask-vs-conclude and the action code
nodes.rationale: Supervisor wants the paper's fine-tune used and mentors want a dedicated semantic-search model; taken explicitly against research note 0001's recommendation, with its findings restated unsoftened in the risk register.

nodes.label: Evidence statements (evidence.csv rows rendered as retrievable sentences)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: evidence statements (evidence.csv rows rendered as retrievable sentences)
nodes.rationale: With TriageEngine gone, a bare (condition, feature, value, strength) tuple means nothing to a language model unless rendered as a sentence; tagged passage_type=evidence_statement so citations trace back to the row.

nodes.label: matching_conditions capped at five
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.rationale: An uncapped bootstrap run named all 18 authored conditions on almost every conclusion because most conditions have no eliminating row; a list that long is the roster, not a differential.

nodes.label: red_flag_id and matching_conditions mutually exclusive (red flags name no condition)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: red_flag_id and matching_conditions mutually exclusive (red flags name no condition)
nodes.rationale: Generalises the cancer-omission rule to every red flag: escalate on a symptom pattern without asserting what it is.

nodes.label: Red-flag recall changes from a provable 100% gate to a measured rate
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: red-flag recall changes from a provable 100% gate to a measured rate
nodes.rationale: The gate was checkable because code evaluated every clause; once escalation depends on the model noticing injected text it is a benchmark rate, so make eval must report rather than assert == 1.0.

nodes.label: red_flags.yaml injected in full every turn, never retrieved
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: red_flags.yaml injected in full every turn, never retrieved
nodes.rationale: Retrieval is approximate and nothing guarantees a red flag is in the top-k hits; injection maximises the chance the model notices, but 100% recall stops being a code guarantee.

nodes.label: TriageDecision schema: the one deterministic safety net left (closed vocabularies via guided decoding)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: triagedecision schema: the one deterministic safety net left (closed vocabularies via guided decoding)
nodes.rationale: The model cannot emit a feature_id, action_code or condition_id outside its closed vocabulary; which question or action it picks within that vocabulary is no longer checked by code.

nodes.label: EMERGENCY exception: matching_conditions allowed beside red_flag_id only at EMERGENCY
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: emergency exception: matching_conditions allowed beside red_flag_id only at emergency
nodes.rationale: Product judgement, not evidence the old rule was wrong: someone sent to an emergency department with only 'seek emergency care now' has nothing to say about why she is there. URGENT_SAME_DAY red flags keep the restriction.

nodes.label: gold_seeds_styled.csv: 540 single-turn QA rows, none a clarifying question
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: gold_seeds_styled.csv: 540 single-turn qa rows, none a clarifying question
nodes.rationale: Mechanical explanation of the clarification collapse to 0.000: the model reproduced a training distribution in which every assistant turn is a finished answer.

nodes.label: NHS citable_only structurally bars fine-tuning on the corpus behind the red flags
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: nhs citable_only structurally bars fine-tuning on the corpus behind the red flags
nodes.rationale: There is no may_be_ingested flag inside a weight matrix; Crown-copyright text in weights cannot be filtered, audited or removed.

nodes.label: Patient-facing urgency recommender sits outside the FDA CDS carve-out regardless of what computes it
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: patient-facing urgency recommender sits outside the fda cds carve-out regardless of what computes it
nodes.rationale: All four section 520(o)(1)(E) criteria are HCP-facing, so keeping the controller does not confer non-device status; the argument for it is inspectability, not compliance.

nodes.label: Verdict: replacing the controller with an end-to-end LLM is contradicted by every primary evaluation found
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: verdict: replacing the controller with an end-to-end llm is contradicted by every primary evaluation found
nodes.rationale: The best-performing systems for clinical question-asking (MediQ) and triage accuracy (MECR-RAG) both added external structure around the model; fine-tune reuse and a semantic-search model are supported without removing the controller.

nodes.label: Instruction is not a mechanism for question-asking
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: instruction is not a mechanism for question-asking
nodes.rationale: MediQ measures that directly prompting a model to ask degrades performance, and the current design's only mechanism for asking is prompt text in DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.

nodes.label: Safety-first metric table (groundedness, citation correctness, safe abstention, robustness)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: safety-first metric table (groundedness, citation correctness, safe abstention, robustness)
nodes.rationale: Aggregate accuracy previously masked unsafe under-triage in this project, so every rate is reported with numerator, denominator and failure IDs.

nodes.label: Two-page NHS-grounded evaluation protocol (24 synthetic cases, three runs, two reviewers)
nodes.community_name: Research 0001: Reconsidering the deterministic controller (LLM triage architecture)
nodes.norm_label: two-page nhs-grounded evaluation protocol (24 synthetic cases, three runs, two reviewers)
nodes.rationale: A small reproducible grounding-and-safety evaluation for the Phase-1 report; 24 synthetic prompts cannot establish diagnostic accuracy, so the claim is bounded to source grounding and preserving explicit help-seeking instructions.

nodes.label: Brand primary colour #9F1239 (--primary in globals.css)
nodes.rationale: Everything on the site is themed to it; an off-palette illustration looks pasted on, so unDraw's colour picker must be set to this value before download.

nodes.label: Illustration component (renders nothing when the file is missing)
nodes.norm_label: illustration component (renders nothing when the file is missing)
nodes.rationale: No broken-image icon and no reserved gap: every layout is built to read correctly with the art absent, so the illustrations are optional and can be added in any order.
nodes.source_location: Nothing breaks if you skip this

nodes.label: Licence-driven source exclusions (NICE CKS, RCOG, ACOG, UMLS) per CLAUDE.md
nodes.norm_label: licence-driven source exclusions (nice cks, rcog, acog, umls) per claude.md

nodes.label: unDraw licence (free use, no bulk collection or redistribution)
nodes.norm_label: undraw licence (free use, no bulk collection or redistribution)
nodes.rationale: Generous about use (free, commercial or not, no attribution) but forbids compiling or distributing assets in packs, automated or manual, without consent.

nodes.label: Illustrations README — download these by hand
nodes.norm_label: illustrations readme — download these by hand
nodes.rationale: Explains why the unDraw illustrations must be fetched manually and kept out of git, how to theme and name them, and that the app degrades gracefully without them. Note: the opening line says 'five SVGs' while the table and closing text say nine files.

nodes.label: Guideline: pick calm, uncluttered illustrations
nodes.rationale: The audience is often worried and sometimes in a hurry; busy art reads as noise.

nodes.label: Filename contract: Illustration resolves name to /illustrations/<name>.svg
nodes.norm_label: filename contract: illustration resolves name to /illustrations/<name>.svg
nodes.rationale: The exact filename in the table is the only link between a downloaded file and its placement; a 404 on the curl check means the filename does not match.

nodes.label: Rule: illustration SVGs stay out of git
nodes.norm_label: rule: illustration svgs stay out of git
nodes.rationale: Committing the SVGs to a real repository is arguably distributing them. The project already excludes NICE CKS, RCOG, ACOG and UMLS over licence wording, so taking a new licence grey area for decoration would be inconsistent.

nodes.label: Nine downloads fill eleven placements (welcome and sources reused)
nodes.norm_label: nine downloads fill eleven placements (welcome and sources reused)
nodes.rationale: welcome.svg covers onboarding step 1 and the dashboard; sources.svg covers onboarding step 4 and the landing page. Nothing else is reused because the same drawing twice inside one flow reads as a placeholder.

nodes.label: Rule: no script, build step or agent may fetch the illustrations
nodes.norm_label: rule: no script, build step or agent may fetch the illustrations
nodes.rationale: The unDraw licence clause names automated downloading explicitly, so curl, a build step or an agent acting on the user's behalf is out; a person must download them by hand.

nodes.label: Accounts bounded context (CONTEXT.md)
nodes.rationale: Authored ahead of the code: terms were settled in design before the schema existed, so the schema could be written in the language rather than the language reverse-engineered from a schema. Accounts depends on Triage; Triage does not depend on it.

nodes.label: Unverified: French coverage and reproductive-health domain transfer
nodes.norm_label: unverified: french coverage and reproductive-health domain transfer

nodes.label: services/model: vLLM serving bge-m3 plus base model with QLoRA adapter
nodes.norm_label: services/model: vllm serving bge-m3 plus base model with qlora adapter

nodes.label: CPU-only services/model: bge-m3 embedding and one search endpoint
nodes.norm_label: cpu-only services/model: bge-m3 embedding and one search endpoint

nodes.norm_label: live test finding: ungrounded base model fabricated citations (acog, mayo clinic) and concluded-and-asked at once

nodes.label: Provenance cap: fallback-only grounding may not resolve to SELF_CARE
nodes.norm_label: provenance cap: fallback-only grounding may not resolve to self_care

nodes.label: A DECLINE does not conclude the consultation
nodes.norm_label: a decline does not conclude the consultation

nodes.norm_label: risk: scope is judged by the model (false refusal is under-triage; unmeasured)

nodes.norm_label: live failure: 'who won world cup 2026' answered as self_care citing a real cbc sentence

nodes.label: Age band derived at read time by triage.age_bands, never stored
nodes.norm_label: age band derived at read time by triage.age_bands, never stored

nodes.label: Risks: weaker privacy stance, plaintext health_notes.content, unmeasured anchoring on the note
nodes.norm_label: risks: weaker privacy stance, plaintext health_notes.content, unmeasured anchoring on the note

nodes.label: An INFORM renders as an ordinary chat bubble and keeps the session active
nodes.norm_label: an inform renders as an ordinary chat bubble and keeps the session active

nodes.label: Risk: inform-versus-triage boundary judged by the model; unmeasured; ungrounded prose surface
nodes.norm_label: risk: inform-versus-triage boundary judged by the model; unmeasured; ungrounded prose surface

nodes.label: Corpus justifies a ~0.6B self-hosted encoder; no serving-time reranker; no hosted API
nodes.norm_label: corpus justifies a ~0.6b self-hosted encoder; no serving-time reranker; no hosted api

nodes.label: Answer-language problem: locale absent from the contract (CrossRAG, multilingual RAG literature)
nodes.norm_label: answer-language problem: locale absent from the contract (crossrag, multilingual rag literature)

nodes.label: ADR 0010: Multilingual embeddings beat Arabic-specific ones; the chunk is a sentence
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: multilingual embeddings beat arabic-specific ones; the chunk is a sentence

nodes.label: ADR 0012: API-hosted reasoning model and a guarded web-search fallback
nodes.norm_label: adr 0012: api-hosted reasoning model and a guarded web-search fallback

nodes.label: ADR 0013: An EMERGENCY conclusion may name matching conditions
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013: an emergency conclusion may name matching conditions

nodes.label: ADR 0014: An off-scope message is declined, not triaged
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014: an off-scope message is declined, not triaged

nodes.label: ADR 0015: A user may keep a date of birth and one health note
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: a user may keep a date of birth and one health note

nodes.label: ADR 0016: An in-scope question may be answered informationally
nodes.norm_label: adr 0016: an in-scope question may be answered informationally

nodes.label: Alsubhi et al., Optimizing RAG Pipelines for Arabic (arXiv:2506.06339)
nodes.norm_label: alsubhi et al., optimizing rag pipelines for arabic (arxiv:2506.06339)

nodes.label: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less (arXiv:2405.09673)
nodes.norm_label: lora learns less and forgets less (arxiv:2405.09673)

nodes.label: MMTEB (arXiv:2502.13595): best public multilingual embedder has 560M parameters
nodes.norm_label: mmteb (arxiv:2502.13595): best public multilingual embedder has 560m parameters

nodes.label: BAAI/bge-m3 as the embedding model
nodes.rationale: On Alsubhi et al.'s Arabic RAG results multilingual encoders beat Arabic-specific ones (BGE-M3 70.99 vs Arabic-MPNet 45.92); the 0.68-point margin over e5-large is not decisive, so the tie was broken by trilingual breadth and MIT licensing.

nodes.label: Reranker deferred (bge-reranker-v2-m3 candidate)
nodes.rationale: Reranking helps when first-stage retrieval lacks semantic precision; the corpus is small. Revisit only when evaluation shows the right passage retrieved but ranked outside top k.

nodes.label: Sentence-aware chunking (the chunk is a sentence)
nodes.norm_label: sentence-aware chunking (the chunk is a sentence)
nodes.rationale: Benchmark corroborates it (74.78 average) but the real reason is structural: every source_quote must appear verbatim and make verify-quotes checks that, so a quotable sentence must exist as a retrievable unit.

nodes.label: cited_passages and RetrievedPassage.url (citations resolve to quoted text and a real link)
nodes.norm_label: cited_passages and retrievedpassage.url (citations resolve to quoted text and a real link)
nodes.rationale: A list of content hashes is useless to a person; resolved eagerly and persisted because retrieval is a live similarity search. An unresolved url stays None, never a constructed URL, which would be a fabricated citation.

nodes.label: Guarded web-search fallback (domain-restricted, robots-checked, never persisted, tagged)
nodes.norm_label: guarded web-search fallback (domain-restricted, robots-checked, never persisted, tagged)
nodes.rationale: More retrieval cannot fix a citation invented because the corpus has nothing; the fallback is the answer to 'the corpus has nothing here', chosen over silent ungrounded generation. Accepted gap: a response can go out before any human has read the page it cites.

nodes.label: ReasoningClient implemented against OpenRouter chat-completions
nodes.rationale: Self-hosting the reasoning model on rented GPU (vast.ai smoke test) is not sustainable for iterative development; Qwen3.5-9B via OpenRouter is orders of magnitude cheaper, and ReasoningClient being a Protocol keeps the provider swappable.

nodes.label: DecisionType.DECLINE (rationale only; all other fields forbidden; exempt from grounding)
nodes.norm_label: decisiontype.decline (rationale only; all other fields forbidden; exempt from grounding)
nodes.rationale: A refusal was unrepresentable, so the model had to CONCLUDE and attach the top retrieved passage; forbidding rather than omitting fields makes 'declined and assigned an urgency' unconstructible, a schema guarantee rather than a prompt hope.

nodes.label: Scope defined as what conditions.yaml, features.yaml and red_flags.yaml can ground
nodes.norm_label: scope defined as what conditions.yaml, features.yaml and red_flags.yaml can ground
nodes.rationale: Keeps a refusal provable against the files rather than a matter of taste; the same closed vocabulary everything else is bounded by.

nodes.label: users.date_of_birth stored on the user (asked at sign-up, nullable)
nodes.norm_label: users.date_of_birth stored on the user (asked at sign-up, nullable)
nodes.rationale: Age is load-bearing (age_band separates perimenopause from PCOS over 45) and re-asking it costs a turn; a stored band would go stale on a birthday at exactly the boundary that matters. Existing users are not hard-gated because that would deny urgency guidance.

nodes.label: Health note (health_notes table, one optional row per user, deletable alone)
nodes.norm_label: health note (health_notes table, one optional row per user, deletable alone)
nodes.rationale: A date of birth is demographic; free text about her health is clinical, so it lives beside the user, not on her, preserving the Accounts glossary. The word 'history' is avoided.

nodes.label: Known background rendered into the system prompt, not the transcript
nodes.norm_label: known background rendered into the system prompt, not the transcript
nodes.rationale: A synthetic user turn would be a lie in an auditable record; the note is framed as unverified, not a current symptom, and unable to fire a warning sign on its own.

nodes.label: DecisionType.INFORM (answer from cited passages, no urgency, no red flag, no matching conditions)
nodes.norm_label: decisiontype.inform (answer from cited passages, no urgency, no red flag, no matching conditions)
nodes.rationale: 'What is PCOS?' fits none of ASK, CONCLUDE or DECLINE, so a legitimate move was unrepresentable. It is the narrowest shape because it could be used to walk around triage: no action_code means it can never function as reassurance, and citations are mandatory.

nodes.label: Prompt rule: a message describing her own symptoms is triaged, never explained; if unclear, ask
nodes.norm_label: prompt rule: a message describing her own symptoms is triaged, never explained; if unclear, ask
nodes.rationale: The schema cannot distinguish 'what is endometriosis?' from 'I think I have endometriosis, what is it?'; informing on a symptom report is under-triage, so the tie resolves toward asking.

nodes.label: vLLM multi-LoRA serving (--enable-lora, --lora-modules, per-request model)
nodes.rationale: Makes 'use the paper's model' and 'do not let it decide urgency' simultaneously satisfiable: the adapter phrases text while the action code comes from Python.

nodes.label: Agentic RAG loop (retrieve, reason, ask or conclude, repeat)
nodes.norm_label: agentic rag loop (retrieve, reason, ask or conclude, repeat)
nodes.rationale: A triage conversation is several questions building to one conclusion, which single-lookup RAG does not fit; its best-known failure (stopping too early) is the under-triage risk the project already measured.

nodes.label: Embedding / semantic search model (bge-m3)
nodes.rationale: A model dedicated to search, kept separate from the reasoning model, as the industry mentors asked.

nodes.label: Licensing filter at live search time (unfinished)
nodes.norm_label: licensing filter at live search time (unfinished)
nodes.rationale: NHS text may be quoted with credit but not copied wholesale; the tag is checked at index build but the per-search check had to be finished before launch.

nodes.label: Retrieval index (source sentences + evidence.csv rows as sentences)
nodes.norm_label: retrieval index (source sentences + evidence.csv rows as sentences)

nodes.label: Worked example: sudden severe pelvic pain -> EMERGENCY
nodes.norm_label: worked example: sudden severe pelvic pain -> emergency

nodes.label: Triage system prompt (never diagnose, one question at a time)
nodes.norm_label: triage system prompt (never diagnose, one question at a time)
nodes.rationale: It is an instruction, not a guarantee: nothing in code checks the model followed it, so compliance must be measured.

nodes.label: TriageDecision structured output schema (ask / conclude)
nodes.rationale: A strict form checked by code so the model cannot invent a fifth urgency level or an undefined question; it cannot stop the model picking the wrong allowed option.

nodes.label: Defect: internal identifiers and disclaimer leaked into user-facing text
nodes.norm_label: defect: internal identifiers and disclaimer leaked into user-facing text
nodes.rationale: A prompt-level rule was violated and no code-level check enforces it.

nodes.label: Defect: first question had no discriminating value
nodes.norm_label: defect: first question had no discriminating value
nodes.rationale: The closed vocabulary constrains which questions exist, not which is useful.

nodes.label: Immediate EMERGENCY on pelvic_pain_with_shoulder_tip_pain with no question asked
nodes.norm_label: immediate emergency on pelvic_pain_with_shoulder_tip_pain with no question asked

nodes.label: scripts/publish-index.sh and the build-index workflow
nodes.rationale: Refuses any index with quote-only passages, the wrong model name or a mismatched bge-m3 revision.

nodes.label: Source.may_be_cited vs Source.may_be_ingested
nodes.rationale: A licence may grant quoting but not redistribution; the split lets NHS back red-flag rules while staying out of the corpus.

nodes.label: matching_conditions capped at 5, never alongside a red flag
nodes.norm_label: matching_conditions capped at 5, never alongside a red flag
nodes.rationale: An uncapped run named 18-19 conditions on almost every conclusion because few rows argue against anything; a whole-roster list looks like an answer without being one. Red flags escalate on a pattern without asserting what it is.

nodes.label: red_flag_id field on TriageDecision
nodes.rationale: A reply driven by the danger list has no retrieved fact to cite because the danger list is never searched; writing a real worked example caught the gap.

nodes.label: NHS is quote-only (citable_only)
nodes.rationale: Crown copyright with no reuse grant; a licence constraint enforced by the validator, important because NHS backs many rows and all red flags.

nodes.label: Schema guarantees a decision is representable, not well judged
nodes.norm_label: schema guarantees a decision is representable, not well judged
nodes.rationale: Both observed defects share this cause; it is a known, documented property of the current architecture.

nodes.label: The NHS decision: no NHS text in S3 or any image (--exclude-quote-only)
nodes.norm_label: the nhs decision: no nhs text in s3 or any image (--exclude-quote-only)
nodes.rationale: NHS content is citable_only; the runtime filter already ranked only ingestable passages, so excluding at build time gives the same results while keeping the text out of deployed artefacts.

nodes.label: Conversational dataset format (messages with role/content)
nodes.rationale: Dialogue data is a sequence of role-tagged messages rather than a flat string, so multi-turn user/assistant exchanges are representable and a chat template can be applied.

nodes.label: TRL dataset types (language modeling, prompt-only, prompt-completion, preference, unpaired preference, stepwise supervision)
nodes.norm_label: trl dataset types (language modeling, prompt-only, prompt-completion, preference, unpaired preference, stepwise supervision)

nodes.label: Tool-calling datasets (tools column, tool_calls, get_json_schema)
nodes.rationale: SFT with tool calling needs a tools column of JSON schemas because the chat template uses it to construct the system prompt; tool arguments need the Json() feature type as they are arbitrary JSON.

nodes.label: assistant_only_loss / completion_only_loss
nodes.rationale: Loss is computed only on assistant turns (or only on completion tokens), ignoring user and system messages; assistant_only_loss needs generation keywords in the chat template.
nodes.source_location: Train on assistant messages only / Train on completion only

nodes.label: Automatic chat-template application to conversational datasets
nodes.norm_label: automatic chat-template application to conversational datasets
nodes.rationale: When given a conversational dataset the trainer applies the model's chat template itself; the EOS token must be aligned with the template (eos_token in SFTConfig) so responses terminate correctly.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning (token-level cross-entropy / NLL)
nodes.rationale: SFT minimises the negative log-likelihood of the target sequence given the input, with a one-token label shift and padding masked by ignore index -100; the model learns exactly what the input/output pairs demonstrate.

nodes.label: backend CI workflow
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: Kept separate from the data workflow because the HTTP and database tests need the api extra and a real PostgreSQL in Docker; path-filtered so a frontend or model change does not trigger it.

nodes.label: data CI workflow (lint, test, validate knowledge, trace consultations)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: data ci workflow (lint, test, validate knowledge, trace consultations)
nodes.rationale: Path-filtered so a frontend or model change does not trigger it. Runs the fast offline suite (contracts, data, triage core).

nodes.label: deploy workflow (production deploy to the single EC2 host)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: deploy workflow (production deploy to the single ec2 host)
nodes.rationale: Images are tagged with the git SHA, never latest. Rollback by hand is git revert on main through the same pipeline. terraform apply is deliberately not here. The workflow runs no tests, so backend and data must be required status checks on main or untested code deploys.

nodes.label: frontend CI workflow (npm ci, build, reporting-only lint)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: frontend ci workflow (npm ci, build, reporting-only lint)
nodes.rationale: The frontend had no PR-time checks before this; services/frontend/** appeared only in deploy.yml, so a change could be discovered only after merge. npm run build is the real gate and type-checks as part of its run. There is deliberately no unit-test step because no test runner is configured.

nodes.label: hygiene workflow (repo hygiene check on every branch)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: hygiene workflow (repo hygiene check on every branch)
nodes.rationale: The checker is stdlib-only with no setup-python, uv or lockfile: a guard against a supply-chain mistake should not itself pull in a supply chain.

nodes.label: JupyterHub idle culling kills the server and rotates the token
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: jupyterhub idle culling kills the server and rotates the token

nodes.label: scripts/check_repo_hygiene.py: five hygiene rules
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: A third-party scanner would mean trusting another supply chain to fix a supply-chain problem; five stdlib rules are auditable in one sitting, each written against something that actually happened.

nodes.label: The history purge with git filter-branch, verified in a mirror
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: the history purge with git filter-branch, verified in a mirror
nodes.rationale: filter-repo and BFG need a network fetch; filter-branch ships with git and is adequate for 123 commits and one path.

nodes.label: Branches still carrying the payload
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup

nodes.label: Issue 1: foreign crypto/blockchain code injected into postcss.config.mjs
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: issue 1: foreign crypto/blockchain code injected into postcss.config.mjs
nodes.rationale: The signature of git add -A in a working directory holding another project's files; unrelated Ethereum code executing in the frontend build is unacceptable whether or not the detection is a true positive.

nodes.label: Issue 2: backend.env.bak committed with live credentials
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: issue 2: backend.env.bak committed with live credentials

nodes.label: Re-infection was a merge of a stale branch, not malware
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: re-infection was a merge of a stale branch, not malware
nodes.rationale: No npm lifecycle hooks exist, so nothing was re-writing the files; a merge resolution took the infected side.

nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: The container filesystem is wiped on every restart and only the home volume survives.

nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: rotate the openrouter key, session secret and jupyterhub token
nodes.rationale: Rotation is the only step that actually protects the credentials; a key that sat in a GitHub repo should be assumed scraped.

nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.rationale: The frontend previously had no PR-time checks; it was only built after a merge to main.

nodes.label: The .gitignore glob gap (*.env did not match .env.bak)
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: the .gitignore glob gap (*.env did not match .env.bak)
nodes.rationale: The no-secrets rule was right; only the glob was wrong, so *.bak and *.env.bak were added.

nodes.label: hygiene.yml workflow with no path or branch filter, plus pre-commit hook
nodes.community_name: Security 0001: injected postcss payload and leaked env backup
nodes.norm_label: hygiene.yml workflow with no path or branch filter, plus pre-commit hook
nodes.rationale: The offending paths matched none of the existing filters and the payload survived on stale branches a main-only check would have passed.
